units.en: His frugal disbursements displeased the army. Regional Commander He Chun impeached him for rigidity, and he was ordered to Beijing to await reassignment.
units.literal: Because his disbursements were frugal, this was inconvenient for the army; Regional Commander He Chun impeached him for rigidity, and he was ordered to come to the capital to await another appointment.

units.zh: 尋授直隸布政使。
units.en: He was soon appointed treasurer of Zhili.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed provincial treasurer of Zhili.

units.zh: 九年，英兵犯大沽，為僧格林沁擊退。
units.en: In Xianfeng 9 the British attacked Dagu and were driven off by Senggelinqin.
units.literal: In the ninth year, English troops attacked Dagu and were beaten back by Senggelinqin.

units.zh: 戰後將議撫，命文煜從總督恆福赴北塘相機辦理。
units.en: After the battle, as peace talks began, Wen Yu accompanied Governor-General Hengfu to Beitang to handle affairs as circumstances required.
units.literal: After the battle, when appeasement was to be discussed, Wen Yu was ordered to follow Governor-General Hengfu to Beitang to handle matters as circumstances allowed.

units.zh: 尋擢山東巡撫。
units.en: He was soon promoted to governor of Shandong.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to governor of Shandong.

units.zh: 捻匪圍曹縣，分黨擾安陵，檄曹州鎮總兵郝上庠合師內外夾擊，解曹州圍，安陵賊亦退。
units.en: Nian bandits besieged Caoxian and raided Anling. He ordered Regional Commander Hao Shangxiang to attack from inside and outside, lifted the siege of Caoxian, and drove off the Anling raiders.
units.literal: Nian bandits besieged Caoxian and split forces to harass Anling; he ordered Caozhou garrison Regional Commander Hao Shangxiang to join armies inside and outside in a pincer attack, lifted the siege of Caozhou, and the rebels at Anling also withdrew.

units.zh: 十年，捻匪又竄單縣，分擾嶧縣得勝徬，遣將擊走之。
units.en: In Xianfeng 10 the Nian raided Shanxian and harassed Desheng Embankment in Yixian; he sent generals and drove them off.
units.literal: In the tenth year, Nian bandits again raided into Shanxian and split forces to harass Desheng Embankment in Yixian; he sent generals and drove them off.

units.zh: 英法聯軍踞砲台，文煜遣兵扼利津，自駐濰縣韓亭以防陸路北犯。
units.en: When the Anglo-French allies held the batteries, Wen Yu posted troops at Lijin and stationed himself at Hanting in Weixian to block a northern land advance.
units.literal: The Anglo-French allied armies held the batteries; Wen Yu sent troops to hold Lijin and himself stationed at Hanting in Weixian to guard against a land route invasion from the north.

units.zh: 尋敵船北駛犯北塘，文煜分軍入衛，駐通州，自率眾赴濟寧剿捻匪。
units.en: When enemy ships sailed north to attack Beitang, he sent troops to defend the capital, held Tongzhou, and personally led forces to Jining against the Nian.
units.literal: Soon enemy ships sailed north and attacked Beitang; Wen Yu divided troops to enter the capital guard, stationed at Tongzhou, and personally led forces to Jining to suppress Nian bandits.

units.zh: 十一年，署直隸總督，尋實授。
units.en: In Xianfeng 11 he acted as governor-general of Zhili and soon received formal appointment.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, he served as acting governor-general of Zhili, and soon received formal appointment.

units.zh: 時和議既成，穆宗回鑾，畿輔馬賊四起，久未淨絕，屢詔責文煜搜捕。
units.en: Peace had been made and the Tongzhi Emperor returned to Beijing, but mounted bandits plagued the capital region for years. Edicts repeatedly ordered Wen Yu to hunt them down.
units.literal: At the time peace had been concluded and the Muzong Emperor returned to the capital; mounted bandits rose everywhere in the capital region and long went uncleared; edicts repeatedly rebuked Wen Yu to search and capture them.

units.zh: 同治元年，坐山東降賊張錫珠等擾畿南督剿不力，褫職，戍軍台。
units.en: In Tongzhi 1 he was dismissed for failing to suppress surrendered Shandong rebels Zhang Xizhu and others who raided south of the capital, and was sent to garrison duty.
units.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, because surrendered Shandong rebels Zhang Xizhu and others harassed the southern capital region and he was ineffective in supervising suppression, he was stripped of office and sent to garrison duty at the military colonies.

units.zh: 二年，僧格林沁奏調赴營差遣，尋授鑲黃旗蒙古副都統。
units.en: In Tongzhi 2 Senggelinqin requested his transfer to camp service, and he soon became vice commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.
units.literal: In the second year, Senggelinqin memorialized to transfer him to camp for assignment; soon afterward he was appointed vice commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.

units.zh: 三年，命赴甘肅慶陽督辦糧台，以病請解職回旗。
units.en: In Tongzhi 3 he was ordered to supervise the grain depot at Qingyang, Gansu, but illness led him to resign and return to his banner.
units.literal: In the third year, he was ordered to go to Qingyang in Gansu to supervise the grain depot; on grounds of illness he requested relief from office and return to his banner.

units.zh: 七年，起授正藍旗漢軍都統，尋出為福州將軍。
units.en: In Tongzhi 7 he was restored as commander of the Han Plain Blue Banner, then posted as general of Fuzhou.
units.literal: In the seventh year, he was restored and appointed commander of the Han Army of the Plain Blue Banner; soon afterward he went out as general of Fuzhou.

units.zh: 十年，兼署閩浙總督。
units.en: In Tongzhi 10 he also served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
units.literal: In the tenth year, he additionally served as acting governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

units.zh: 十三年，日本兵船窺伺台灣，偕總督​​李鶴年、船政大臣疏陳防務。
units.en: In Tongzhi 13 Japanese warships threatened Taiwan. With Governor-General Li Henian and the naval affairs minister he memorialized on coastal defense.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, Japanese warships watched for an opportunity against Taiwan; together with Governor-General Li Henian and the minister of naval administration he memorialized on coastal defense.

units.zh: 光緒三年，入覲，留京授內大臣、鑲白旗漢軍都統、左都御史，擢刑部尚書。
units.en: In Guangxu 3 he came to audience, stayed in Beijing as imperial body minister, commander of the Han Bordered White Banner, and left censor-in-chief, and was promoted to minister of Punishments.
units.literal: In the third year of Guangxu, he came to audience, remained in the capital, was appointed imperial body minister, commander of the Han Army of the Bordered White Banner, and left censor-in-chief, and was promoted to minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 七年，協辦大學士。
units.en: In Guangxu 7 he became associate grand secretary.
units.literal: In the seventh year, he became associate grand secretary.

units.zh: 九年，充總管內務府大臣。
units.en: In Guangxu 9 he supervised the Imperial Household Department.
units.literal: In the ninth year, he served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household Department.

units.zh: 十年，拜武英殿大學士，以病乞罷。
units.en: In Guangxu 10 he became Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall and retired on grounds of illness.
units.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall and requested retirement on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 尋卒，贈太子少保，諡文達。
units.en: He died soon after and was posthumously titled Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Wenda.
units.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Wenda.

units.zh: 兩江總督曾國荃等奏文煜咸豐中孤軍捍賊，保全裡下河，請於揚州建專祠，允之。
units.en: Governor-General Zeng Guoquan and others memorialized that in the Xianfeng era Wen Yu held off rebels with a lone force and saved the Lixia River region, and asked for a temple at Yangzhou; the court agreed.
units.literal: Governor-General Zeng Guoquan of the Two Jiangs and others memorialized that in the Xianfeng era Wen Yu with an isolated army resisted rebels and preserved the Lixia River region, requesting a special temple at Yangzhou; this was approved.

units.zh: 子志顏，理籓院侍郎。
units.en: His son Zhiyan served as vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
units.literal: His son Zhiyan was a vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

units.zh: 論曰：桂良以帝室葭莩，與聞軍國，數膺議和之使，無所折衝。
units.en: The historians comment: Gui Liang, as an imperial in-law, took part in military and state affairs and undertook repeated peace missions, yet achieved no diplomatic success.
units.literal: The judgment states: Gui Liang, by virtue of kinship with the imperial house through marriage, took part in military and state affairs and repeatedly received missions to negotiate peace, yet achieved no diplomatic success.

units.zh: 瑞麟從僧格林沁勦賊防夷，曾著勞勚。
units.en: Rui Lin campaigned with Senggelinqin against rebels and foreigners and once rendered notable service.
units.literal: Rui Lin followed Senggelinqin in suppressing rebels and guarding against foreigners and once rendered notable service.

units.zh: 文煜亦處兵間，無功可錄。
units.en: Wen Yu also saw military service but left no achievement worth recording.
units.literal: Wen Yu also was amid warfare, yet had no achievement worth recording.

units.zh: 官文雖無過人之才，推賢讓能，奠安江漢，與曾國籓、胡林翼和衷規畫，竟完戡定之功。
units.en: Guan Wen lacked surpassing talent but deferred to able men, secured the Yangzi heartland, and planned in harmony with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi to complete the pacification.
units.literal: Guan Wen, though without surpassing talent, deferred to the worthy and yielded to the able, settled and secured the Jiang and Han regions, and with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi planned in harmony, ultimately completing the achievement of pacification.

units.zh: 茅土同膺，旂常並煥，豈諸人所可並語哉？
units.en: They alike received fiefs and enfeoffment, their honors shining together—how can the others be mentioned in the same breath?
units.literal: They alike received fiefs and enfeoffment, their banners and tablets shine together—how can the others be spoken of in the same breath?
